newsitem.title: USA: Florida pleased with tobacco RICO ruling.
newsitem.headline: Florida pleased with tobacco RICO ruling.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles said Friday he was pleased with a ruling by Palm Beach County Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen that allows the state to pursue racketeering claims against the tobacco industry.

"For decades, the tobacco cartel has conspired -- like a crime family -- to hook our people on its deadly product and hide the evidence," Chiles alleged in a statement. "The truth will come out when we get to trial in August. When we win, the tobacco barons will pay a heavy price for putting their profits ahead of our people and the truth."

Earlier Philip Morris Cos Inc issued a statement saying that Cohen's ruling was not a reflection on the merits of the case. It said that it would become clear going forward that Florida would be unable to support the allegations.

If Florida were to win its claims against tobacco companies under the state's Racketeer Influence and Corrupt Organizations Act, the more than $1 billion in damages it is seeking from tobacco companies could be tripled to more than $3 billion, and set a precedent for other states.
Florida has filed suit against the industry, seeking reimbursement for public funds used to provide health care for people with tobacco-related illnesses.
